resources.string: Detects when you open an app you have locked so Biometric App Lock can ask for your fingerprint. It reads which app is in the foreground. On package-installer, Settings, and device-admin screens it also reads the on-screen text to see if an uninstall, force stop, clear storage, or device-admin deactivation targets a locked app or Biometric App Lock. If you cancel the fingerprint prompt, it closes that system screen. It does not read what you type.
A few system settings are still off. Setup opens each screen for you.
Each step opens the right system screen. Turn the setting on, then come back. The next step opens on its own.
You\'re set. You can change these later from Review setup.
That settings screen could not be opened on this phone.
Add a fingerprint. This app will not open its settings or unlock apps without one. On the next screen, choose Fingerprint and follow the steps.

Android blocks the accessibility switch for apps installed from a file until you allow it. On the app info screen, tap the three-dot menu in the top corner, then Allow restricted settings. Confirm, then come back. If you do not see that menu item, the switch is probably already available.

Turn Biometric App Lock on. If you land on a list, open Installed apps or Downloaded apps, then Biometric App Lock, and switch it on. If the switch is greyed out, go back, open app info, tap the three-dot menu, and choose Allow restricted settings.
This asks Android to refuse uninstalling Biometric App Lock until you turn device admin off. On the next screen, tap Activate. It does not lock the phone or wipe it. You can skip this.

This phone has Samsung Auto Blocker. This app could not read whether it is on, so check the screen. This is a manual check.

App locking still works while Auto Blocker is on. Leave each switch on unless it is stopping something you are doing.

Block apps from unauthorized sources stops installing or updating this app from an APK file. Galaxy Store and Play Store installs are not blocked. On some One UI 7 and newer phones, a Safe install warning can still appear for an APK even when that switch is off. Install anyway continues the install. That warning is separate from Auto Blocker.

Block commands by USB cable stops the computer setup commands. Setup on the phone does not use those commands.

Maximum restrictions, on One UI 6.1.1 and newer, blocks device administrator. Uninstall protection cannot be turned on until Maximum restrictions is off. Message links, 2G, Wi-Fi, shared albums, and photo location under that setting do not affect this app.

Malware-image blocking, app scans, and blocking unofficial system updates do not affect this app.
Auto Blocker is on. App locking still works. Leave every switch on unless a line below says it is stopping something you are doing.
The main Auto Blocker switch reads as off, but a switch below still reads as on. Check the screen before changing anything.
This app could not read the main Auto Blocker switch.

Block apps from unauthorized sources is on. That stops installing or updating this app from an APK file. Galaxy Store and Play Store installs are not blocked. Turn that switch off only while you install from a file, then you can turn it back on. On some One UI 7 and newer phones, a Safe install warning can still appear after the switch is off. Install anyway continues the install.

Block apps from unauthorized sources is off, so an APK install is not blocked by that switch. On some One UI 7 and newer phones, a Safe install warning can still appear. Install anyway continues the install. That warning is separate from Auto Blocker.
This app could not read Block apps from unauthorized sources. If an APK install is refused, that is the switch that does it. Store installs are not blocked.
Block commands by USB cable is on. That stops the computer setup commands. Leave it on if you are setting this up on the phone.
Block commands by USB cable is off, so the computer setup commands are not blocked by that switch.
This app could not read Block commands by USB cable. If the computer setup commands fail, that is the switch that does it. Setup on the phone does not need it.

Maximum restrictions is on. That blocks device administrator, so uninstall protection cannot be turned on until Maximum restrictions is off. App locking still works. The other items there do not affect this app. Leave them on.
Maximum restrictions is off, so device administrator can still be turned on.

This app could not read Maximum restrictions. On One UI 6.1.1 and newer that switch blocks device administrator, which uninstall protection needs. If the screen has no Maximum restrictions row, this phone does not have that extra block.
This One UI version is older than 6.1.1, so Maximum restrictions is not on this phone.
Malware-image blocking, app scans, and blocking unofficial system updates do not affect this app. Leave them on.
The button opens Auto Blocker. If this phone has no direct shortcut, it opens Security settings. Then tap Security and privacy, then Auto Blocker.
Allow unrestricted battery so the lock is not stopped in the background. On the next screen, tap Allow. If you get a list instead, open Biometric App Lock and choose Unrestricted. You can skip this.
No fingerprint is enrolled. Add one in Settings → Security → Fingerprint.
This device has no fingerprint sensor (or it is unavailable).
Fingerprint authentication is unavailable right now.
Confirm your fingerprint to view or change which apps are locked.
These settings stay locked until a strong biometric is available. Existing app locks are unchanged.\n\n%1$s
The previous key was revoked. Authenticate to set app lock up again.
Fingerprint enrollment changed. App lock now uses your current fingerprints.
Authentication could not be verified. Nothing was unlocked.
The secure hardware key could not be used. Nothing was unlocked.
Asks for a fingerprint before uninstall, force stop, or clear storage.

When this is on, uninstalling a locked app or Biometric App Lock asks for your fingerprint. Force stop and clear storage for those apps ask too. Android also refuses to uninstall this app until its device administrator is turned off, and that screen asks for your fingerprint. The accessibility service has to be on for those prompts. Device administrator is used only to block uninstalling this app. It does not lock the phone, wipe data, or change other settings. Turning this switch off removes the device administrator. You have already confirmed your fingerprint to open this screen.
Made by Achilles Rogan. Opens the GitHub page.
No browser is installed, so the GitHub page could not be opened.
Biometric App Lock uses device administrator only so Android will not uninstall this app until you turn it off. It will not lock the screen, wipe the phone, or change other settings.
Uninstall protection is on. Deactivating device admin lets Biometric App Lock be uninstalled.
Could not change uninstall protection. Nothing was changed.
Uninstall protection will not see uninstall screens until the accessibility service is on.
Confirm with your fingerprint to continue. Cancel returns you to the home screen and stops this action.
